rationale:
Identity verification was correctly done via name and ZIP. However, there are multiple policy violations and factual errors:

1) The agent executed the helmet exchange without first stating the exact change and obtaining explicit confirmation. Policy requires explicit confirmation before any order-changing write.

2) The agent wrongly refused the customer’s request to exchange the delivered luggage set. They cited a fabricated rule (“only one exchange per delivered order”) and incorrectly claimed the helmet and luggage were in the same order. In fact, the helmet was in #W3947049 and the luggage set was in #W6876713, so an exchange for the luggage set should have been permitted.

3) When the user asked to return the luggage set, the agent described the change but immediately proceeded to submit the return without explicitly obtaining the user’s confirmation after restating the details, again violating the confirmation requirement.

4) The pending grill modification was handled correctly: the agent requested explicit confirmation, verified variants, and performed the modification with accurate final information.

Because of the unconfirmed writes and the incorrect refusal based on wrong facts and unsupported policy, the conversation fails the pass bar.
